description: Pipe-content identification colour schemes, transcribed from the sources in ../sources.md. The standards are paywalled; every row is a public fact repeated by the cited extracts. Colours are NAMED categories. A standard never fixes an sRGB value (ANSI Z535.1 / RAL / BS 4800 define physical colours, several outside sRGB), so the display hex lives in llull_display_palette.json and is a llull choice, never a gate.
gradeLegend: A = two or more independent extracts agree; B = one extract, or extracts conflict; C = located only

asme_a13_1.standard: ASME A13.1 Scheme for the Identification of Piping Systems (colour scheme in force since the 2007 edition, oxidizing added to the yellow class in 2015; editions 2020 and 2023 cited by vendors)
asme_a13_1.note: A13.1 colours a MARKER (label band) on the pipe, not the pipe. Plant-review tools tint the whole pipe by service; llull does both (display tint + optional marker decals). Field = background of the marker, letters = legend text colour.

rows.contents: fire-quenching fluids (water / foam / CO2 for fire suppression)

rows.conflict: S2 (projectmaterials chart) prints white letters on orange; field colour agrees in all three

rows.contents: flammable fluids and oxidizing fluids (oxidizing added in 2015)
rows.conflict: S2 assigns flammable to brown/white and only oxidizing to yellow; S1 and S3 (J.J. Keller, Brimar 2015 summary) agree on yellow/black for both

rows.contents: potable, cooling, boiler feed and other water

rows.conflict: S3 (Brady) lists purple/white, white/black, brown/white, black/white as the four user pairs; S1 lists purple, gray or black backgrounds with white letters

unresolved: Steam / hot water: one vendor extract gives 'gray field, black letters' for steam, condensate, boiler feedwater and other hot water; another gives white/black. Not used as a gate (grade C).

asme_a13_1_legend_size.standard: ASME A13.1 (vendor tables cite the 2007 / 2015 editions)
asme_a13_1_legend_size.basis: outside diameter of pipe OR covering (insulation included), inches

rows.grade: A (letter height) / B (length: S6 Brady brochure prints 5 in)

placement.rule: markers at valves and flanges, at changes of direction, at branches, on both sides of wall / floor / ceiling penetrations, and at intervals on straight runs; flow arrows, both directions where flow reverses
placement.straightRunSpacing: conflicting: 25-50 ft (Brady, 2007), 20-25 ft (Safety Media), 25 ft (Brimar, 2023) -> llull default 25 ft = 7620 mm, named default, grade B

asme_a13_1_legend_size.gaps: The interval band between 1.25 and 1.5 in, 6 and 8 in OD is not covered by the vendor tables (edition differences). llull maps an OD in a gap to the next larger row and reports `bandInterpolated: true`.

iso_14726.standard: ISO 14726:2008 Ships and marine technology - Identification colours for the content of piping systems (confirmed 2024)
iso_14726.note: Main colour = group of media; one or two additional colours distinguish media in a group (e.g. potable water blue-green-blue, condensate blue-yellow-blue per the DIN ISO 14726 abstract). Not for medical gases, industrial gases or cargo.

bs_1710.standard: BS 1710 Specification for identification of pipelines and services (2014 edition; one vendor cites 2019)
bs_1710.note: Basic identification colour bands with BS 4800 references; safety colours added on top of the basic colour.

rows.contents: oils - mineral, vegetable or animal; combustible liquids
gases in either gaseous or liquefied condition (except air)

safetyColours.meaning: fresh water from a public supply (auxiliary)

din_2403.standard: DIN 2403 Kennzeichnung von Rohrleitungen nach dem Durchflussstoff (2014-06 referenced by TRGS 201; later editions withdrawn / in draft)
din_2403.note: Group colour per medium, as tabulated by TRGS 201 Anhang 3. One extract only: documentation, not a gate.
